author: nana-ec
body:
Signed-off-by: Nana-EC <nana.essilfie-conduah@hedera.com>

**Description**:
The `transactions.js` logic utilizes heavy inner and outer queries to provide results to the `api/v1/accounts` and `api/v1/transactions` endpoints.
These queries are inefficient with multiple joins and don't lend themselves to distributed querying.

In #2273 it was possible to modify the queries to improve performance, this change adopts those improvements

- Convert transaction sub query to CTE, with support for an additional CTE when transactions need to be further filtered
- Break out transfer tables into separate CTEs to support distribution
- Utilize CTE result for base of transactions and avoid extra join on transaction table again
- Rename transaction table `consensus_ns` column to standard `consensus_timestamp`

**Related issue(s)**:

Fixes #2676 

**Notes for reviewer**:
Performance results after runs against a local db with a large data set (~6.5 million transactions at ~1.5 GB).
Summary: There's a slight improvement in response times of around 500-1000ms on average.
Slowest times are improved and the distribution of times is more narrow and smaller.
Additionally, the structure of queries support multi node distribution so we should see even more improvements  in such an environment.

author: dougmacknz
body:
# Objective
Sets MenuItem flex-basis to `auto` instead of 100%. 

The parent for this component (MenuContent) is a flex container with flex-direction: column, meaning this trying to set each item to be 100% height.

This was only manifesting in TitleBlockZen, where there's a container around MenuContent that was set to display: flex. I've switched that to display block now as well as an additional safety measure. There's no reason for it to be a flex box.

# Motivation and Context
Closes https://github.com/cultureamp/kaizen-design-system/issues/1915

author: hintak
body:
The test case in issue 20 uncovers 3 problems:

- Microsoft compiler treats %s passed to *w*printf(), different from everybody else. So we need to special-case Microsoft compiler with one wide-string-format specifier, and everybody else with a different one. (and vice versa for narrow string - but there is only one case, in main()).

- After fixing the truncation, I found a missing null termination problem with the previous work-around for unix systems lacking a wctime() function (and need to call ctime() then convert from narrow to wide).

- and a similar problem with earlier long to int32_t, needs to replace a lot of %li by %i to not implicit convert to 64-bit long.

I only replaced %li in TTEngine.cpp ; the other seems to affect user messages (if error) and not critical.

author: evildave666
body:
Originally when the S2 Mini board was brought up, there was some discussion as to whether or not to include an I2C singleton for it, as there was no explicit marking for such on the silkscreen for the board.

However, the S2 Mini is designed to be pinheader compatible with the ecosystem of shields for the Lolin/Wemos D1 Mini, and that does have a standard for I2C (they produce at least 6 shield boards using this standard as well as a board that provides a qwiic-like connector for several display boards, all using the same pin assignments).

The tipping point for me was when jepler pointed out to me on discord the designation of SCL/SDA pins directly from the schematic.

So therefore I'm submitting this PR to add a board.I2C singleton.

Tested with the Lolin TFT I2C Connector Shield and a 128x64 OLED board using the qwiic-like interface from this shield as well as a 64x48 oled shield.

author: codex-
body:
Just a small set of project improvements based on what I saw at first glance when going to implement some features.

- @types are dev deps, not real deps, unless exported explicitly as a part of a package to be consumed.
- Updated the gitignore with things that were immediately generated and then git tracked.
- Abstracted the eslint rules out to a dedicated `.eslintrc.json`
  - Sorted / organised the file.
  - Added section to handle the JS config explicitly.
    - Means you can avoid the copy paste ignores.
  - Added `@typescript-eslint/await-thenable` & `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises`.
    - These two warn on what in my experience is one of the most common sources for bugs in applications.
- Improve the CICD workflows.
  - Bump to use latest `setup-node`.
  - Run lint / build and every commit.
  - Only generate artifacts for PR's (original behaviour).
- Update use of deprecated webpack config.

author: github-learning-lab[bot]
body:
# Using `request changes` on a pull request Thanks again for all your help on that last pull request. With our powers combined, _anything_ is possible! This next change might introduce some new changes that aren't going to look great. Sometimes, the author might identify that something isn't working. They might need a helping hand :wave: to solve the problem. In other instances, it might only work in their environment. When reviewing a pull request, look at and test the code to pinpoint any bugs or unexpected behavior. ### Writing a review #### Review the `diff` Reviewing the `diff`, the comparison of the proposed code, in the context of the whole project. Could it introduce performance problems, or security vulnerabilities? Try to predict unintended consequences that this change could cause. #### Try it out For most things, actually trying out the proposed change is a good idea. This makes it a lot easier to tell if the actual change matches the intention. You can do this by: - Cloning the repository, and checking out to the branch compared in the pull request. Run the application in your local development environment. - Deploying the pull request to a review-lab or staging environment (as appropriate). When summarizing your review, let the author know if you completed any of these tests. #### Empathy and Constructive Feedback The goal of providing feedback on a pull request is to ensure that the best possible change is being added. Sometimes, a change isn't addressing the problem in the best possible way. It's the reviewer's responsibility to provide meaningful and constructive feedback. ### Requesting Changes 101 Before you submit your review, your line comments are pending and only visible to you. You can edit pending comments anytime before you submit your review. To cancel a pending review and its pending comments, scroll down to the end of the page in the Conversation tab. Then click **Cancel review**. ## Step 4: Leave a review that asks for changes If you could check out this code for me and tell me what is wrong, that would be fantastic. ### :keyboard: Activity: Requesting changes 1. On the pull request, click **Files changed** 1. Hover over the line of code where you'd like to add a comment, and click the blue comment icon 1. In the comment window, type your comment 1. Click **Start a review** - If you have already started a review, you can click **Add review comment** 1. Above the changed code, click **Review changes** 1. Type a comment summarizing your feedback on the proposed changes - _Note: The problem here is that too many Tetris pieces are the same color. In your review, you might want to suggest that I choose colors which would be easier to see when playing the game._ 1. Select **Request changes** to submit feedback introducing changes necessary before merging 1. Click **Submit review**

Return to this pull request for my next comment

> _Sometimes I respond too fast for the page to update! If you perform an expected action and don't see a response, wait a few seconds and refresh the page for your next steps._

author: brandones
body:
Create tests for the configurability of the extension system. These live in esm-framework, because they depend on esm-config, esm-extensions, and esm-react-utils. This also includes some minor refactoring.

The potentially contentious thing introduced here is `debug`. Have a look at the [docs](https://github.com/visionmedia/debug#readme). You enable it in node (for tests) with an env variable `DEBUG=openmrs:xyz`, or in the browser with `localStorage.debug = 'openmrs:xyz'`.

I imagine integrating this into esm-framework to make it easier to debug state changes, config loading, extension attachments, etc. Probably we'd want to codemod it out of production builds. We'd also need to be quite careful that it isn't misused or overused, or it could become really annoying to anyone who wants to use it (remember how LoggingAdvice in OpenMRS Core logged every function entrance and exit at level INFO for like 5 years and everyone hated it?). Your thoughts and suggestions are welcome.

author: teor2345
body:
## Motivation

Zebra's mempool only adds verified transactions when it gets a new request.
But there is no guarantee that peers or the crawler will send requests regularly enough for transaction propagation.

This is unexpected work in sprint 20.

### Specifications

Transaction propagation behaviour isn't specified.

We assume that transactions should propagate across the network every target block interval.

## Solution

- Add a `CheckForVerifiedTransactions` mempool request
  - Document existing requests and responses
  - Part of ticket #2859
- Modify the existing tests to use `CheckForVerifiedTransactions` as the dummy request
- Spawn a `QueueChecker` task to check for newly verified transactions
  - Update the `start` command documentation for the mempool
  - Part of ticket #2859

This PR is based on PR #2887, because they change the same code.

## Review

Anyone can review this PR, I just tried to pick someone who wasn't busy.

### Reviewer Checklist

  - [ ] Code implements Specs and Designs
  - [ ] Tests for Expected Behaviour
  - [ ] Tests for Errors

author: geod24
body:
```
Most calls to `getValidators` are done for the current (or next) height,
and historical data are rarely looked up.
We can take advantage of this by caching based on the height,
to reduce the number of memory allocations or database lookups.
```

I'm a bit on the fence about this, since it can defeat some expectations (as seen in `addPreimages` invalidation).
But we call this method a lot and either we need to start passing the array around, or caching like here.

author: xirov
body:
fixes #2622 
fixes #2812

Requires a bit of manual setup (since we skip the installation step) when running with docker-compose.

1. Find the `deviceId` and `apiKey` for Syncthing in the syncthing configuration file, in the syncthing container:
```
docker-compose exec syncthing sh
vi /var/syncthing/config/config.xml
```

2. In the backend container insert the following in `/etc/ucloud/syncthing.yaml`:
```
syncthing:
  sharedSecret: sync-mounter-secret
  devices:
    - hostname: syncthing
      apiKey: <apiKey>
      id: <deviceId>
      port: 8384
      username: syncthinguser
      password: syncthingpassword

syncMount:
  deviceId: <deviceId>
```

3. Run the migrations:
    - `file-orchestrator-service` -> `V15__Sync.sql`
    - `file-ucloud-service` -> `V10__Sync.sql`

4. Insert product category with type `SYNCHRONIZATON` into `product_categories`, and product into `products`

author: samsondav
body:
This introduces a new pattern for ORM methods that aims to clarify usage and remove some common footguns, notably:

1. It should be easy and obvious how to pass a parent context or a transaction into an ORM method
2. Simple queries should not be cluttered
3. It should have compile-time safety and be explicit
4. It should enforce some sort of context deadline on all queries by default
5. It should optimise for clarity and readability
6. It should mandate using sqlx everywhere, gorm is forbidden in new code
7. It should make using sqlx a little more convenient by wrapping certain methods
8. It allows easier mocking of DB calls (Queryer is an interface)

The two main concepts introduced are:

A `Q` struct that wraps a `sqlx.DB` or `sqlx.Tx` and implements the `postgres.Queryer` interface.

This struct is initialised with `QOpts` which define how the queryer should behave. `QOpts` can define a parent context, an open transaction or other options to configure the Queryer.

A sample ORM method looks like this:

```golang
func (o *orm) GetFoo(id int64, qopts ...postgres.QOpt) (Foo, error) {
  q := postgres.NewQ(q, qopts...)
  return q.Exec(...)
}
```

Now you can call it like so:

```golang
orm.GetFoo(1) // will automatically have default query timeout context set
orm.GetFoo(1, postgres.WithParentCtx(ctx)) // will wrap the supplied parent context with the default query context
orm.GetFoo(1, postgres.WithQueryer(tx)) // allows to pass in a running transaction or anything else that implements Queryer
orm.GetFoo(q, postgres.WithQueryer(tx), postgres.WithParentCtx(ctx)) // options can be combined
```

author: jaormx
body:
Currently, when dealing with node scans, we only allow the scan to go
forward if the node is not unschedulable (via the unschedulable flag of
the Node object). However, for public cloud cases where there might be a
lot of ephemeral nodes (e.g. when a node autoscaler is being used), this
is not ideal as it's very difficult to do scans. On the other hand, if a
node became unready while the scan was on-going, we also return a
similar error.

So, to deal with this, the PR introduces the option `strictNodeScan`,
which enables an administrator to toggle whether we want to be strict
when getting results of a scan.

The default is `true`, which is the setting we were using before.
However, when set to `false`, the scan will not fail if a node is set to
`unschedulable` and will ignore "unschedulable" errors on the scan pods.
Thus allowing us to still get a subset of scans.

Signed-off-by: Juan Antonio Osorio Robles <jaosorior@redhat.com>

## Changelog Entry
To be copied to the [draft changelog](https://github.com/vgteam/vg/wiki/Draft-Changelog) by merger:

 * (Nothing that concerns the user)

## Description

Added a multithreaded version of `rebuild_gbwt()`. The user partitions the graph into an appropriate number of jobs based on (sets of) weakly connected components and provides a mapping from node ids to job ids. Each job consists of a set of subpath mappings and an estimate of the size of the job (typically the total size of the components). The jobs are started in decreasing order by size, and the number of parallel jobs can be specified in the parameters. Each job produces a temporary GBWT, and the temporary indexes are merged using the fast algorithm.

author: pavel-esir
body:
**Problem statement**: Some `TF` models contain `IteratorGetNext` node instead of `Parameter`, previously we suggested user to cut it by manually specifying `--input ...` but this can be done automatically. This is needed in order to support Out Of the Box (OOB) conversion for mixnet-l, and efficientnet models family.

**Solution**: Added front transformation `IteratorGetNextCut` which finds all nodes with `IteratorGetNext` and cuts them replacing each output port by `Parameter`. Transformation `IteratorGetNextCut` reuses exactly the same mechanism as `input_cut.py` from the front phase.

**Important notes**: old scenarios of conversion will not be affected: if either `--intput ...` or `--input_shape ...` are specified transformation will not run.

Ticket: xxx-60963

Code:
* [x]  Comments
* [x]  Code style (PEP8)
* [x]  Transformation generates reshape-able IR
* [x]  Transformation preserves original framework node names: **original FW IteratorGetNext node names cannot be preserved since they are cut out**

author: aloisklink
body:
The `grpc.cmake` file has been upgraded.

-DBUILD_GRPC_LIB=ON
===================

Firstly, if we are downloading GRPC from GitHub, we are now
including GRPC into our CMake environment.

This lets all CMake config pass over to compiling GRPC,
letting us cross-compile.

However, since GRPC requires a protoc and grpc_plugin_protc
compiled on the host already,
cross-compiling doesn't work on Ubuntu 20.04.

(`apt install protobuf-compiler-grpc` installs a version
 that is too old for GRPC v1.36.4)

-DBUILD_GRPC_LIB=OFF (default)
==============================

So, additionally, I've added a feature to find a pre-existing
GRPC install, using CMakeModules/FindgRPC.cmake

This works with an `apt install libgrpc++-dev` version of cmake,
and should work for cross-compilation (in theory).

```Elixir
# Text rotation.
sheet7 =

  |> Sheet.set_cell("A1", "Hello - angle_ccw",  text_rotation: :angle_ccw)
  |> Sheet.set_cell("B1", "Hello - angle_cw",  text_rotation: :angle_cw)

```xml
    <xf numFmtId="0" fontId="0" fillId="2" borderId="1" xfId="0" applyFill="1" applyBorder="1" applyAlignment="1">

```

author: mec
body:
## Changes in this PR
Welcome traveler! 🧙 

This is the first step on a jounrney towards a more modular set of models to allow the applicaiton to export data.

The first step was to define the BEIS approved strings for as many `Activity` attributes as I could find - I rely on these in the second commit. I am not going for perfection here, there may be some unneeded strings, we can tighten then up as we go and have wider work for that planned on https://trello.com/c/bf9t1om8

Next I introduce a model that sets a pattern for more to  follow. the detail is in the commit message, but basically the idea is these model can produce an entire column or set of related columns of data that can then be rendered into a csv.

These building block classes are glued together by Activity ID just like in the database.

What I like about this is that it abstacts getting the data into the shape we want - as you can see here this can result in much cleaner code, it allows us to reuse the classes in different exports, it will let us mix up columns, I also consider it more approachable and simpler to test the individual classes - all good stuff.

To help visualise how this will work in practice, imagine a `ActivityActualSpendColumns` class, and then:

```ruby
activities = Activity.all
attributes = [:roda_identifier, :delivery_partner_identifier]

activity_data_column = Export::ActivityAttributesColumns.new(activities: activities, attributes: attributes)
actual_spend_column = Export::ActivityTransactionColumns.new(activities: activities

headers = activity_data_column.headers + actual_spend_column.headers

rows = activities.map do |activity|
  activity_data_column.rows.fetch(activity.id) + actual_spend_column.rows.fetch(activity.id)
end
```

Now your service object, controller or whatever you want can create the csv file from the `header` and `rows` data.

author: ahurlbatt
body:
## Description

<!-- If this is a bug-fix or enhancement, state the issue # it closes -->
<!-- If this is a new feature, reference what paper it implements. -->

If the estimation of a geometric transform matrix is overdetermined, meaning there are more pairs of source and destination points than required (e.g. more than 4 points in 2D), then the total least squares method will return a matrix that performs best on average for each of the point pairs. Depending on the source of information on the point pair locations, it might be that more confidence can be placed in some pairs, and less in others. 

To allow such a situation to be specified, this addition allows a vector or list of weights to be provided, where each element corresponds to a combined weight for each for each pair of points. After a normalisation to the range [0, 1], these weights are square rooted and built into a diagonal matrix, by which the coefficient matrix A is multiplied. This follows from the treatment of variances in conventional least squares methods. The relative values of the weights could therefore be considered as inverse variances for each point pair.

By providing and using weights in this manner, points for which the position is known with a lower confidence can be given a smaller weighting to have less influence over the final transformation matrix.

author: fmrsabino
body:
- Rustup introduced a new format to declare the toolchain version on `1.23.0` – https://blog.rust-lang.org/2020/11/27/Rustup-1.23.0.html#new-format-for-rust-toolchain
- The old format can still be used for backwards-compatibility reasons

Note: `rustup show active-toolchain` results in something like:
```
nightly-2021-05-21-aarch64-apple-darwin (overridden by '/safe-client-gateway/rust-toolchain.toml')
```

So I'm using `cut -d " " -f1` to get the actual toolchain name

- This can be removed once https://github.com/actions-rs/toolchain/issues/126 is fixed

## Summary
Module:Subbobject removes fields that won't be saved to lpdb right after subobject processing. I think this is done too early in the process, so I moved the culling to right before the lpdb calls are made.

This allows passing non-lpdb fields between subobject processing and match processing. And reduces the risk of fields inadvertently added to subobjects during match processing.

## New Project

Initial approach follows Ecto instrumentation, recording spans for all Redix `[:redix, :pipeline, :stop]` events.

The command sanitization is inspired-by and adapted from [Java instrumentation][1], from where I've also copied the actual commands and what configuration should they follow.

Network attributes are tracked via a "sidecar" process, which keeps track of connection attributes also via `telemetry`. This extra bit of bookkeeping is needed as command events doesn't include that piece of information, unfortunately.

author: davidwalschots
body:
## Summary of Changes
Decreases time spent on reading and writing variables from the Rust system simulation code to MSFS. This resulted in one frame's system calculation time reducing from 400 microseconds to 135 microseconds on my machine. More importantly, it scales better as the size of systems code grows. Replaced `HashMap` and `HashSet` usages with `FxHashMap` and `FxHashSet` for another decrease to 112 microseconds.

Performance is improved by removing lots of `String` allocations. This is done by moving the `String` to MSFS variable mapping to the initialisation phase. Determining the target of a read/write is thereafter done by an index lookup in two `Vec`s. Thus removing the need for `HashMap<String, AircraftVariable/NamedVariable>` (very expensive) or `HashMap<VariableIdentifier, AircraftVariable/NamedVariable>` (slightly expensive).

**In summary, this PR provides a 3.57x performance increase on system simulation code.**

Thanks to @SparkyPotato for pointing out the variable read/write issue and giving their thoughts on it.

## Code review
- `systems/src/simulation/mod.rs` and `systems_wasm/src/lib.rs` contain the most important changes.
- Hydraulic test style is different from other tests. There I've done some hasty changes to make it work. In the future these tests should start using the `SimulationTestBed` throughout. I've discussed this with @crocket63. I've also flagged the `UpdateContext::new` function as deprecated, to serve as a continuous reminder.
- I've made sure to add an `InitContext` this time around, to make any future cross-cutting concern changes in the initialisation phase easier to add. Having to modify function signatures every time is a pain!

author: pandom79
body:
**What is this ?**

I thought to a notification service about the upgrade of the packages.
The service works like the others services eg. tar_scm, download_url, etc ...
It's a simple python script which uses a html parser to retrieve all versions of a package determining the newer versions than the current.
It'a an indipendent service, therefore it can be also used by debian, arch packager etc..
The comparing's algorithm has been written following the general rules of linux software versioning.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_versioning

**Why ?**

The reason is simple: after created a package, a packager could forget it.
In the best case, after having remember to update it, he has to go to its web page and to check if a newer version exists
or subscribe himself to mailing list/newsletter of the upstream project.
Maybe after read that email, could forget to update it anyway...We read many emails to the day!
At this point, I asked myself if an automatic mechanism was possible to do that in which we always can see if an upgrade is required for that package to avoid forget it.
This PR makes exactly that.

**How does it work?**

As written above, it's a python script which uses a html parser.
it depends by python and its requests module.

Following a configuration example:

```
<services>
    <service name="check_upgrade">
        <param name="urlsrc">https://github.com/openSUSE/open-build-service/releases</param>
        <param name="regexurl">/openSUSE/open-build-service/archive/refs/tags/[\d].[\d]+.[\d]+.tar.gz</param>
        <param name="regexver">[\d].[\d]+.[\d]+</param>
        <param name="currentver">2.10.4</param>
    </service>
</services>
```

The service makes a http get request to "**urlsrc**" and parsing the http response extracting the version data according
"**regexurl**" pattern. After that, for each value, we extract only the version according "**regexver**" pattern and comparing it
with the "**currentver**" (which pattern must also match "regexver") parameter value to determine if the value represents a newer version than current, creating
a file called "**_service:check_upgrade:newer_versions**" which will contain all the newer versions.
Moreover, the "**separator**" parameter value, which value is "." as default, can be useful for particular cases.

This is an example:

```
<service name="check_upgrade">
	<param name="urlsrc">https://www.jetbrains.com/pycharm/whatsnew/</param>
	<param name="regexurl">/pycharm/whatsnew/[\d]+-[\d]+/</param>
	<param name="regexver">[\d]+-[\d]+</param>
	<param name="currentver">2019-1</param>
	<param name="separator">-</param>
</service>
```

This example show how the parser can retrieve whatever data....not only href tag.
You can find the "check upgrade" service and examples [here](https://github.com/pandom79/obs-service-check_upgrade
).
A packager will can test it locally via osc command, after that, will upload it on OBS.
A this point, there was the "refresh" problem of this service which i resolved via Active job.
Now, when we will show our home project, for each package will show the "Upgrade" label is a newer version exist.
Going into the package, we can see the "_service:check_upgrade:newer_versions" file content to see which are the newer versions.

**Personal opinion**

I'm trying this feature on my obs instance and it's working like a charm but.....
Unfortunately I see that the obs service generates always a new revision also when the source are identical.
If I wrong, feel you free to suggest me the changes.
That means, the active job which will start every 7 days (just an example), it will generate a new revision every 7 days, therefore
an eventual "zypper dup" will ask to update these packages....Well, i'd want to avoid it.
If the "check_upgrade" script works well for you but we cannot resolve the revision problem, i already have another solution in my mind.


**Alternative way**

First of all, the "check upgrade" has not to be an "obs service", but a simple script instead.
The active job will scan all packages, for each of them,
will check if a "_job" (just an example) file exists which content could be:

```
<jobs>
    <job name="check_upgrade">
        <param name="urlsrc">https://github.com/openSUSE/open-build-service/releases</param>
        <param name="regexurl">/openSUSE/open-build-service/archive/refs/tags/[\d].[\d]+.[\d]+.tar.gz</param>
        <param name="regexver">[\d].[\d]+.[\d]+</param>
        <param name="currentver">2.10.4</param>
        <param name="sendmail">true/false</param>
    </job>
</jobs>
```

I think that because could be there other jobs in the future....

At this point, the active job will run the script and it will can simply to update a field on the Package table called "upgrade" which values can be (true/false).
We will use it in package_datatable.rb
`name << tag.span('Upgrade', class: 'badge badge-info') if record.is_upgrade?
to show the "upgrade" label.
We create another table on db which relations packages and jobs called "packages_job" (just an example) in wchich we store the "check upgrade" script result.
This table could be useful also for other jobs in the future.....
Front end side, when we will entry in an upgradable package,
we can show a new tab next to "RPM Lint" called "Job activities"
where we show the name of job and its result.
For example:

```
Check upgrade
Available the following version for upgrade:
1.2
1.3
and so on....

```
Obviously, here could be there also the results the other jobs such as a summary.
"Send mail" parameter value could be useful if the packager wants be also notified via email.

In this way, we haven't no longer revision problem, therefore less zypper updates.

Final conclusion
I think that a similar mechanism have to be present on this project.
Would be useful for many packager, myself included. If you are interested about that, even if i am absolutely new to ruby, rails, perl and docker, i can develop it.

Regards

author: marusak
body:
When the initial load of the last 12 hours does not return any data
then after one minute when we try to update the last minute we load all
the data there is.
The updating logic calls `load_data` with `this.most_recent`. This variable
has initial value `0` and is updated when some data are parsed.
Calling `load_data(0)` translates to loading all the data it can find.

Fixes #16462

author: richardjgowers
body:
Fixes #3437

Changes made in this Pull Request:

The string interning we're using for string TopologyAttrs uses a more complex system than just a numpy array of values.  `Topology.add_Residue` and `Topology.add_Segment` previously just assumed a numpy array of values, so blindly "appended" values to this without respecting fancy data structures.

The fix is to add `_add_new` to each TopologyAttr which is a respectful way of appending to the TopologyAttr.

author: mattcaswell
body:
This PR fixes 3 different problems:

- engine reference mishandling in pkey_set_type
- engine reference mishandling in provider_util.c
- dasync bug when using EVP_CIPHER_CTX_copy()

Fixes #16757 
Fixes #16845
Fixes #16844 

This PR is targeting master and 3.0. A backport will need to be done for 1.1.1 (not all issues apply, and some tweaks will be required).

Note: investigating these issues highlighted that we have a behaviour change between 1.1.1 and 3.0 wrt CMAC keys. In 1.1.1 if you attempt to create a CMAC key with EVP_PKEY_new_CMAC_key(), but supply key data that is too short, then we notice this right away. However in 3.0 we don't notice it until you actually try and use the key. This means we'll need to tweak my test during backporting as well.

author: nathanlb
body:
According to [LWC best practices](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/component-library/documentation/en/lwc/lwc.events_best_practices) sending a non-primitive in `event.detail` as we've been doing for facet value selection is not recommended and was creating errors in Community context. 

the initial error was cause by the @api value for `item` which is give to the `CategoryFacetValue` was being passed as value in the event.detail. @api values like this one are wrapped in a [read-only membrane](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/component-library/documentation/en/lwc/lwc.events_best_practices) that threw multiple errors in Community.

With this change the `FacetValue` (CategoryFacetValue & FacetValue) now pass the facet `value` through event.detail. the facet concerned then finds the appropriate value in its members and uses that to execute the headless action for selection.

This also includes a fix for the `no-search` option on the `quanticFacet`. The facet without the search enabled would display an erroneous state without checkboxes. FT was updated to verify that with the fix, the facet displays checkboxes when that option is set.

author: halfflat
body:
* Add test that is sensitive to small radius loss of precision in ixa computation.
* Add test that checks for consistent behaviour when there is an (isolated) zero radius point in the morphology.
* Special case p==1 q==1 case in ratelem so that it can interpolate ixa in the presence of non-finite interpolants.
* Change naming in pw_element/pw_elements: 'element' refers to the extent+value pairs comprising a 'pw_elements' object; 'value' refers to the value associated with an element; 'extent' refers to the closed interval which is the support of the element.
* Allow values (but not extents) in a pw_elements object to be mutable, using proxies for iterator access.
* Write piecewise zip (pw_zip) in terms of a lazy pw_zip_view. Rename zip functions.
* Document pw_elements more thoroughly.
* Simplify and document embed_pwlin.cpp routines, expressing everything in terms of simple interpolate/integrate operations.
* Represent integrated inverse cross-sectional area in the embedding by multiple piecewise-rational functions over a branch, each of which contribute separately to an ixa-based integration, so that precision loss associated with small (or zero) radii can be avoided.
* Comment embed_pwlin.cpp more thoroughly.

Fixes #1526

I'm putting in this PR now since I am taking off or the weekend in a few minutes.

## What is done:

### functionality

- Wallet.ts has a new `handleUxInteraction` property to be set when setting up the wallet. This property is passed to `Account.ts` when an account is 'created'. 
- GasLimit and GasPrice are estimated in the Account.ts if they don't exist. Since Account.ts has access to the provider and the transaction, it makes the most sense to estimate it here rather than passing it to the component to estimate.
- This `handleUxInteraction` is called when a transaction is sent.
- `handleUxInteraction` passes up the chain to context which stores it in its own state
- The transaction is then passed to RootRouter which displays it in the modal
- The user confirms/cancels the transaction which either resolves or rejects the promise created in Account.ts
- The transaction is then cleaned up from context, which hides the modal. *

### UX/UI 

- removed the "review transaction" from the home (src/App.tsx) screen
- added copy button to temp screen.

#### 2. WC version compatible

#### 3. WC Admin enabled

To disable WC_ADMIN, add the following line at the end of functions.php of the active theme:

```add_filter( 'woocommerce_admin_disabled', '__return_true' );```

Expected result: admin error message saying WooCommerce Admin is needed to use WCPAY

After the test, remove the snippet from functions.php

#### 4. WC Admin Version compatible

Install WC ADMIN from the WP plugin repository: https://wordpress.org/plugins/woocommerce-admin/
Downgrade WooCommerce Admin to a version lower than 0.23.2. 

Expected result: admin error message saying WooCommerce Admin needs to be at least version 0.23.2 to work with WCPAY

After the test, disable the WooCommerce Admin plugin.

Expected result: admin error message saying WordPress needs to be updated to work with WCPAY

author: joebingham-wk
body:
## Motivation
  <!-- High-level overview of what you are trying to fix or improve, and why.
         Include any relevant background information that reviewers should know. -->

I ran into an issue where I needed to query a portal that was attached directly to the `document.body` rather than inside of RTL's `container`. Doing research revealed that [this should work out of the box](https://github.com/testing-library/react-testing-library/issues/62#issuecomment-506005319) because queries are bound to [the document.body by default](https://github.com/testing-library/react-testing-library/blob/8f17a2bc4fa9c2c17a623b38ded9ab18b086e457/src/pure.js#L98). We were doing things slightly differently by binding queries to the render result's container, preventing us from being able to access portals like the library anticipates. This PR tweaks that to align with the JS side!

## Changes
  <!-- What this PR changes to fix the problem. -->
- Change the default query bindings to be the render result's `baseElement` instead of `container`
- Update tests

#### Release Notes

         ("Fix bug" and not "Fixed bug" or "Fixes bug.") -->

body:
There is a slight race in checking of a context deadline exceed in #16467
which leads to a 500 on the repository page.

The solution is to check the error coming back from `*LogNameStatusRepoParser.Next()`
and if it is the `ContextDeadlineExceeded` break from the loop.

Fix #17314
Regression #16467

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>

author: coreymasanto
body: VP9 codecs are represented in the form of `"vp09.level.profile.color_depth"`. I had originally wrote differing, random values for the level, profile, and color depth values of the VP9 codec strings used within the test, but many of these strings do not actually represent valid codecs, as confirmed via the empty string returned by [canPlayType()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/canPlayType) when the fabricated codecs are passed in (e.g., `"video/mp4; codecs=vp09.02.30.11"`). This PR updates the test to use a VP9 string that is playable.

author: arbitrary-echo
body:
This handler monitors the price spread ratio (similar to percent error) between the Perpetual Finance price and the FTX price compared to threshold.  There is a time component as well, such that the price must be outside the threshold for some period of time before triggering an alert.

From the Perpetual Finance team:
```
Price spread ratio is outside of the range

author: jamesetsmith
body:
# Summary
Fixes a `cmake` problem that occurs when compiling with GCC and using MKL as the BLAS implementation. When passing ${BLAS_LIBRARIES} to `libcint`, `cmake` splits the variable into a space-delimited list and then `cmake` things some of the library paths are `cmake` arguments and throws an error.

To be clear, this _is not_ a problem with `libcint`'s build system. So building `libcint` on its own with these BLAS/compiler combinations works.

# Original Problem

```
[  5%] Performing configure step for 'libcint'
cd /mnt/home/jsmith/apps/pyscf/pyscf/lib/build/deps/src/libcint-build && /cm/shared/sw/nix/store/581z66lakaimqjgx29rayxxzlnc211mm-cmake-3.21.3/bin/cmake -DWITH_F12=ON -DWITH_RANGE_COULOMB=1 -DWITH_FORTRAN=0 -DWITH_CINT2_INTERFACE=0 -DMIN_EXPCUTOFF=20 -DKEEP_GOING=1 -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=/mnt/home/jsmith/apps/pyscf/pyscf/lib/deps -DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR:PATH=lib -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/cm/shared/sw/nix/store/pnpgpir9ax38kwc4ibfpr7mi4m19m840-llvm-12.0.1/bin/clang -DBLAS_LIBRARIES=/cm/shared/sw/nix/store/lam0yzb5q3rafzjy5d99qlhihwd2b83x-intel-oneapi-mkl-2021.3.0/mkl/2021.3.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_lp64.so 
/cm/shared/sw/nix/store/lam0yzb5q3rafzjy5d99qlhihwd2b83x-intel-oneapi-mkl-2021.3.0/mkl/2021.3.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_thread.so /cm/shared/sw/nix/store/lam0yzb5q3rafzjy5d99qlhihwd2b83x-intel-oneapi-mkl-2021.3.0/mkl/2021.3.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so 
/cm/shared/sw/nix/store/pnpgpir9ax38kwc4ibfpr7mi4m19m840-llvm-12.0.1/lib/libiomp5.so -lpthread -lm -ldl "-DCMAKE_C_CREATE_SHARED_LIBRARY=<CMAKE_C_COMPILER> <CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_C_FLAGS> <LANGUAGE_COMPILE_FLAGS> <LINK_FLAGS> <CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_CREATE_C_FLAGS> -o <TARGET> <OBJECTS> <LINK_LIBRARIES>" -DBUILD_MARCH_NATIVE=OFF "-GUnix Makefiles" /mnt/home/jsmith/apps/pyscf/pyscf/lib/build/deps/src/libcint
CMake Error: Unknown argument -ldl
CMake Error: Run 'cmake --help' for all supported options.
```

## Systems Failing Before Fix
| Compiler Version | BLAS Implementation | Build Success?|
|:--:|:--:|:--:|
|gcc/11.2.0    | intel-mkl/2020.4        | No|
|gcc/11.2.0    | intel-one-api/2021.3 | No|
|gcc/11.2.0    | openblas/0.3.15         | Yes|
|gcc/10.2.0    | intel-one-api/2021.3 | No|
|clang/12.0.1 | intel-one-api/2021.3 | No|
|clang/12.0.1 | openblas/0.3.15         | Yes|

# Fix
Rather than pass build arguments to `libcint` with `CMAKE_ARGS` in `ExternalProject_Add`, we now pass them with `CMAKE_CACHE_ARGS` and treat the list of MKL libraries as a single string, preventing `cmake` from splitting it up.

# Relation to Existing PRs
This PR includes the fix mentioned into PR #1075.

# Next Steps
Let me know if there are any comments/suggestions!

### Description
This PR changes model types across plugins to Golang Time types rather than strings. The purpose is to unify our handling of time and timezones in the store/read process of our data.

### Does this close any open issues?
#426 

### Current Behavior
Some plugins use string types, some use Time types.

### New Behavior
All our plugins use Time types.

### Other Information
1. I have used sql.NullTime types on our models where necessary.
2. I have added a Convert method to change strings received from APIs to sql.NullTimes
3. I have added unit tests for this.
4. I have replaced time.IsZero() functions with an isValidTime function. This is important because this comparison with .IsZero() doesn't function properly with the returns from our Convert methods.

author: apivovarov
body:
This PR adds support for `return_sequences` bool param for [Keras LSTM layer](https://keras.io/api/layers/recurrent_layers/lstm/).
By default the param is False - LSTM returns only the last h output
If `return_sequences is True` then ALL h outputs should be returned. The outputs should be concatenated along axis 1.

I also added dedicated test for LSTM. Input shape increased to test `return_sequences is True` case.

`return_sequences = True` is needed if your model has two or more LSTM layers. By Default LSTM layer takes 3D tensor and returns 2D tensor. To connect two LSTM layers together the first layers should return 3D tensor. It can be achieved if `return_sequences param` set to `True`.

[Understanding LSTM Networks](https://colah.github.io/posts/2015-08-Understanding-LSTMs/)

Related discussion https://discuss.tvm.apache.org/t/keras-lstm-return-sequences-parameter-not-supported/11239

author: sblaisot
body:
3.4.2 CIS detection example is `modprobe -n -v sctp | grep -E '(sctp|install)'`

`MODPROBE_FILTER` is necessary here because `sctp` module depends on `libcrc32c` module so even if it is disabled, `modprobe -n -v sctp` returns

```
insmod /lib/modules/4.19.0-18-cloud-amd64/kernel/lib/libcrc32c.ko 
install /bin/true
```

and detection fails

This PR fixes that behaviour by adding missing `MODPROBE_FILTER` to `is_kernel_option_enabled` call.

author: tigewilliamsaxon
body:
This adds the `min_tls` config setting.  This allows us to specify the minimum TLS version we want to support.  If it is not supplied, then Kurento will not set a minimum TLS version and it will simply use the highest supported version between client and server.

The update also checks the version of OpenSSL that is being used to build Kurento with.  If it is built with a OpenSSL 1.1.0 or later, it will use the new `SSL_CTX_set_min_proto_version` function to set the minimum TLS version.  Older versions of OpenSSL have to manually set the various `SSL_OP_NO_TLS*` flags to turn off TLS versions lower than the specified minimum.

This PR seeks to resolve the performance problems caused by storing rate limit entries in the `wp_options` table (which are by default autoloaded). It introduces a new table, `woocommerce_rate_limits` to accomplish this.

Rate limit lookups are cached upon creation and retrieval, so DB reads should be kept to minimum.

I've included a migration for existing options that haven't expired, though I suspect the scenario to be unlikely unless a 3PD is using `WC_Rate_Limiter` or has filtered the `woocommerce_payment_gateway_add_payment_method_delay` value to be very high.

Additionally, I've included a daily cron job to clean up expired limits.

### How to test the changes in this Pull Request:

1. (On `trunk`) Add a rate limit to a test store with a long delay: `WC_Rate_Limiter::set_rate_limit( 'add_payment_method_1', 99999 );`
2. Check out this branch
3. Run the DB migration
4. Verify that an `add_payment_method_1` row exists in the `woocommerce_rate_limits` table in your database
5. Go to the My Account page
6. Add a payment method
7. Immediately attempt to add another payment method
8. Verify the error that you "tried too soon"

If you're having trouble triggering the rate limit default, use this filter:
```php
add_filter( 'woocommerce_payment_gateway_add_payment_method_delay', function() {
	return 60;
} );
```

body:
https://openedx.atlassian.net/browse/ENT-5045

To not get rate limited while doing bulk expirations, we will use the lms api directly to update course enrollments.

**Merge checklist:**
- [ ] Any new requirements are in the right place (do **not** manually modify the `requirements/*.txt` files)
    - `base.in` if needed in production but edx-platform doesn't install it
    - `test-master.in` if edx-platform pins it, with a matching version
    - `make upgrade && make requirements` have been run to regenerate requirements
- [ ] `make static` has been run to update webpack bundling if any static content was updated
- [ ] `./manage.py makemigrations` has been run
    - Checkout the [Database Migration](https://openedx.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AC/pages/23003228/Everything+About+Database+Migrations) Confluence page for helpful tips on creating migrations.
    - *Note*: This **must** be run if you modified any models.
      - It may or may not make a migration depending on exactly what you modified, but it should still be run.
    - This should be run from either a venv with all the lms/edx-enterprise requirements installed or if you checked out edx-enterprise into the src directory used by lms, you can run this command through an lms shell.
        - It would be `./manage.py lms makemigrations` in the shell.
- [ ] [Version](https://github.com/edx/edx-enterprise/blob/master/enterprise/__init__.py) bumped
- [ ] [Changelog](https://github.com/edx/edx-enterprise/blob/master/CHANGELOG.rst) record added
- [ ] Translations updated (see docs/internationalization.rst but also this isn't blocking for merge atm)

**Post merge:**
- [ ] Tag pushed and a new [version](https://github.com/edx/edx-enterprise/releases) released
    - *Note*: Assets will be added automatically. You just need to provide a tag (should match your version number) and title and description.
- [ ] After versioned build finishes in [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/edx/edx-enterprise/actions), verify version has been pushed to [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/edx-enterprise/)
    - Each step in the release build has a condition flag that checks if the rest of the steps are done and if so will deploy to PyPi.
    (so basically once your build finishes, after maybe a minute you should see the new version in PyPi automatically (on refresh))
- [ ] PR created in [edx-platform](https://github.com/edx/edx-platform) to upgrade dependencies (including edx-enterprise)
    - This **must** be done after the version is visible in PyPi as `make upgrade` in edx-platform will look for the latest version in PyPi.
    - Note: the edx-enterprise constraint in edx-platform **must** also be bumped to the latest version in PyPi.

body:
Ticket: [GEAR-198](https://pcdc.atlassian.net/browse/GEAR-198)

This PR implements highlighting criteria group, i.e. algorithm, based on `isMatched` status in order to help users to examine which part of the matching algorithm contributes to the overall matching status. The toggle button for highlighting is placed under the option menu. 

If the highlight is active, any algorithm with `isMatched` value set to `true` will get light-blue background, while any algorithm with `isMatched` value set to `false` will get light-red background. When parent and child algorithms conflict in their `isMatched` values, the child's value will be used for that part. 

See the following screen recording for demo:

body:
The Codespaces product team has gotten some user feedback that the term
`privacy` field of port forwarding is confusing. Some quick user feedback has
indicated that a term like `visibility` is more clear, e.g. "port 3000 is publicly
visible" rather than "port 3000's privacy setting is public."

We believe that Codespaces is the only user of this term as we're not aware
of it showing up anywhere else (e.g. `devcontainer.json`). Please let me know
if this isn't the case.

This PR is what I believe the minimal change required to change the UI
to show "Visibility" vs "Privacy", though I don't claim that it's
complete (e.g. I am not sure how we handle localization), rather, a
place to start the conversation.

@alexr00, I've been told you are the right person to direct this to, and
would love to chat about this change in more detail.

author: atavakoliyext
body:
The `include` function allows templates to be composed of other templates.

The motivation for this change is to allow composition of complex templates from simpler components. This is currently difficult because the only mechanism available for composing a template from multiple files is the `fileContents` function, which copies contents of files ad-verbatim. This requires that all parameters of the component files are known beforehand, which is often not the case, and does not allow the component templates to use inputs from variables.

Fixes #305

author: jcmustin
body:
## Summary 
This PR adds the end-to-end testing framework Cypress to the code base. It's configured to run with each push via a GitHub action, as well as locally via `yarn cypress-run` and `yarn cypress-open`. For more on creating and running tests, see the testing section at the bottom of README.md. 

This code comes from the following four pull requests, which are all now live on the EA forum:
https://github.com/centre-for-effective-altruism/EAForum/pull/188
https://github.com/centre-for-effective-altruism/EAForum/pull/201
https://github.com/centre-for-effective-altruism/EAForum/pull/216
https://github.com/centre-for-effective-altruism/EAForum/pull/220

## Cypress Setup
1. Create a new remote mongo database. For the EA Forum this db lives within the same instance as our dev database, but it can live wherever.
2. Create a user for your new database with `readWrite` and `dbAdmin` roles. Mongo Atlas offers an easy place to do this.
3. Generate a connection string URI for the database using the username and password generated in step 3.
4. Save that connection string in two places: 
  a) in the LessWrong-Credentials repo under `./connectionStrings/testing-db.txt`, and 
  b) as a GitHub repository secret for this repo, which lives under the Settings tab. Name that secret `TESTING_DB_URL`.
5. Create a file to store your database public settings. For the EA Forum this lives under `ForumCredentials/loadTestingDbSettings.js`. Add the following settings to disable rate limiting:
```
{
  //...
  forum: { 
    postInterval: 0,
    maxPostsPerDay: 100, // much higher than we need now, but it feels like a low cost way to future proof things
  }
  commentInterval: 0,
  // ...
}
```
(note: Currently no tests rely on API keys.)
6. As a one time action, load public settings into the database using `mongo $(< ../LessWrong-Credentials/connectionStrings/testing-db.txt) <path/to/loadTestingDatabasePublicSettings.js>`.

From here, the tests should be runnable both via the GitHub action and locally via yarn commands.

## Notes
Currently the db instance settings file lives within this main repo, under `./settings-test.json`. As I understand so far, accessing this from the Credentials repo during a GitHub action will require storing both the transcrypt key and an SSH token as GitHub repository secrets, which I wasn't terribly excited to do. I suspect there's another option here that I haven't thought of yet, but for now these files don't contain anything confidential.

(Closes https://github.com/LessWrong2/Lesswrong2/pull/1579 😄 )

author: devmotion
body:
This PR replaces NonlinearSolve with Roots for solving the root finding problem in the inverse of the planar layer.

I fixed some type inference problems in Roots some weeks ago (https://github.com/JuliaMath/Roots.jl/pull/245) and some time ago also the convergence and AD issues of this algorithm were fixed by https://github.com/TuringLang/Bijectors.jl/pull/126 by using an improved initial bracket and custom adjoints (BTW the ReverseDiff adjoint was never used and broken, it's fixed in this PR as well); so the motivation and reasons for https://github.com/TuringLang/Bijectors.jl/pull/155 (move from Roots to NonlinearSolve) are gone.

The main motivation for this PR is (apart from the ReverseDiff bugfix) that it reduces the dependencies of Bijectors quite dramatically and hence makes the package more lightweight (https://github.com/TuringLang/Bijectors.jl/issues/199). author: snektron
body:
Adds big integer saturating left shift with 2s-complement semantics, and also updates stage2 to use them. I also uncovered an issue where initializing a big integer with a negative minimum would panic. The previous implementation would compute the number of limbs required from the number of bits, and subtract one for the signed case. This works fine on all but the signed minimum, and so I've updated the way that is computed. This new version also reduces the amount of limbs required to set an integer in some case, for example, `@as(u128, 1)` would now require only 1 limb rather than 2 on a 64-bit platform.

This leaves just a stage-2 compatible version of `__muloti4` required in order to make `saturating_arithmetic.zig` passing, but this requires both `bit_not` and `div_trunc` air instructions.
